name: Joan of Arc
label: Jade Tree
lede: Joan of Arc broke up after its first show, drew a 1.9 from Pitchfork, paired ex-members off by pulling names from a hat and rewrote Orwell with the band in the cast. Tim Kinsella was the only constant for all 25 years.

eras.title: Broke up after the first show
eras.text: When Cap'n Jazz fell apart, Tim Kinsella started again straight away and nearly ended it just as fast. After one gig the band that became Joan of Arc threw out every song, then made a debut that AllMusic said listeners would love or find hideous.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joan of Arc (band) · Wikipedia: Tim Kinsella
years.h: Red Blue Yellow plays one show, then burns every song
years.p: Tim Kinsella's post-Cap'n Jazz band quits after its first gig and throws out the material. Three months later, as Joan of Arc, it plays the Autonomous Zone in Chicago.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account is blunt: the band "broke up after their first show, threw away all of their old material, and started afresh." Kinsella formed it in 1995 after Cap'n Jazz dissolved, and he was its lead singer, main songwriter and only continuous member until the end in 2020.

years.h: Jade Tree signs Joan of Arc off two 7-inches
years.p: The Delaware label was already home to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]] when two early singles landed the band a deal.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Portable Model Of · Wikipedia: Joan of Arc (band)
years.h: A Portable Model Of sets stark acoustic songs against small electronics
years.p: Recorded at Elliot's Loft and Idful Music in Chicago, with [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]] and Ryan Rapsys of Euphone guesting.
years.xp: AllMusic's verdict was that most listeners would either love the record or find it hideous. Wikipedia calls it the album that "introduced Joan of Arc's signature sound": stark acoustic songs combined with subtle electronics.
play: I Love a Woman (Who Loves Me)

eras.title: The laptop takes over
eras.text: Joan of Arc went further into the machine: laptops, samples, songs past 100 tracks. Critics split hard, Jade Tree lost confidence, and in 2001 Kinsella shut the band down and made Owls with his Cap'n Jazz bandmates.

years.h: Jeremy Boyle brings a laptop to How Memory Works
years.p: Synthetic noise and vocal samples cut between the songs. [[Jeremy Boyle|3b67e0f4-9eed-4e5e-bf93-2638afa046c2]] arrives with software work from his art training at the University of Illinois at Chicago.

years.h: Live in Chicago, 1999 is a studio record
years.p: The title only says where the band lived that year. Joan of Arc liked titles and artwork that misled, amused or confused.

years.big: A frustrating, daring and sometimes unlistenable entry in the band's canon
years.h: Pitchfork gives The Gap a 1.9, and Spin gives it an 8
years.p: The Chicago Tribune's verdict on a record built entirely in Pro Tools between October 1999 and June 2000, with some songs past 100 tracks.
years.xp:
The cover nods to Jean-Luc Godard's 1967 film Weekend. PopMatters wondered whether the album "may be one of the most unlistenable albums in existence." Exclaim! took the other side of the argument: "With each album, the band pushes their craftsmanship for the obscure even further."

Tim Kinsella didn't make it easier on himself. In promotional interviews he insisted on asking the questions, which may have added to the bad reviews.

years.h: Joan of Arc calls it quits in May 2001
years.p: Tension in the band, a Jade Tree that has lost confidence and a poorly received EP after The Gap add up to the first breakup.

years.h: Owls puts Cap'n Jazz back together minus one, for a single tour
years.p: Tim Kinsella, [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]], Sam Zurick and [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] release [[Owls|f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2]] on Jade Tree, recorded with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]].
years.xp: Wikipedia describes Owls as a reincarnation of the original Cap'n Jazz lineup without guitarist Davey von Bohlen. The band dissolved after one tour, then reunited in 2012 and released a new album in 2014.

eras.title: Guitars return, and the hat comes out
eras.text: Joan of Arc came back with guitars and grew into a collective of Califone members, cousins and anyone who had ever played in the band. Kinsella moved to Polyvinyl, directed a feature film and kept a second band, Make Believe, going alongside.

yt: Tim Kinsella live, Mercury Lounge, New York, Aug 8 2003
years.h: So Much Staying Alive and Lovelessness brings the guitars back
years.p: Sam Zurick and Mike Kinsella are on it, and nothing about it sounds like The Gap. AllMusic called it a return to form; it's Joan of Arc's last album for Jade Tree.

years.h: Califone produces In Rape Fantasy and Terror Sex We Trust
years.p: A darker, collaged Joan of Arc record from the same sessions, on Perishable, made with [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]]'s [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]] and Ben Massarella.

years.h: Bobby Burg and Nate Kinsella join, and the touring four double as Make Believe
years.p: Tim Kinsella adds bassist [[Bobby Burg|928e4971-5c1a-421a-8ef5-7c1fc74c03b0]] and his cousin [[Nate Kinsella|dee29ad9-ba52-4af1-8372-4acbfb725554]] to Sam Zurick for touring. The same four run [[Make Believe|82d7935d-c121-43e3-8f33-ed999f9357f8]] until 2008.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls Make Believe "2003's touring version of Joan of Arc", though with a more aggressive approach to songwriting than Joan of Arc's.

years.h: Polyvinyl releases Joan of Arc, Dick Cheney, Mark Twain
years.p: The band's first Polyvinyl album brings in a huge team of collaborators and draws some of its best reviews.

years.cap: Joan of Arc Presents Guitar Duets
years.h: Ten ex-members draw partners from a hat for Guitar Duets
years.p: Tim Kinsella gathers ten former members and friends, [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]] among them, pulls names to make pairs and has each pair record a guitar duet. Tracks are identified only by the pair's faces.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joan of Arc (band) · Wikipedia: Tim Kinsella
years.h: Orchard Vale shows Tim Kinsella is also a film director
years.p: His feature, released as Joan of Arc Presents Orchard Vale, opens at the Chicago Underground Film Festival.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts the film as another experimental release for the band, directed by Kinsella.

years.cap: Joan of Arc on stage, July 2008
years.h: Theo Katsaounis joins on drums as Boo! Human takes 14 players
years.p: The Polyvinyl album calls on 14 musicians. [[Theo Katsaounis|31133026-476a-42f5-9d17-5d20f62e93fe]] joins in 2008 and stays behind the kit to the end.

eras.title: Four names on the last album
eras.text: On Joyful Noise, Joan of Arc settled into a steady four-piece and got more conceptual than ever: Bowie sampled into collage, a vocalist who took over the mic, a novel rewritten with the band as characters. In 2020 Kinsella ended it after 25 years.

years.cap: Tim Kinsella singing with Joan of Arc
years.h: Joyful Noise ships ten Joan of Arc albums on cassette
years.p: The box set runs from A Portable Model Of (1997) through Flowers (2009).

years.cap: Joan of Arc at New World, January 27, 2011
yt: Tim Kinsella, in-store at Mojo, Tampa, Jan 2011
years.h: A four-piece Joan of Arc goes back to basics and tours more
years.p: Life Like comes with more regular touring than any recent lineup. The same year Oh Brother collects four albums begun and never finished, with [[Zach Hill|df6a1106-6caf-465b-bcfd-0b80d2b53516]] among the players.

years.cap: Tim Kinsella at Mojo Books & Records, Tampa, January 2011
years.h: Tim Kinsella turns novelist for Featherproof Books
years.p: The Karaoke Singer's Guide to Self-Defense comes out in September. A second novel, Let Go and Go On and On, follows in April 2014, drawn from actress Laurie Bird's 1970s film career.

years.cap: Joan of Arc at Soda Bar, San Diego
yt: Shown and Told, live in Kyoto, Jan 2013
years.h: Melina Ausikaitis joins, and the last lineup is set
years.p: The vocalist and guitarist joins Tim Kinsella, Bobby Burg and Theo Katsaounis. Those four names end up as the title of the final album.

years.cap: Tim Kinsella with Joan of Arc
years.h: A museum hosts Joan of Arc's collage made only of Bowie samples
years.p: Made during Tim Kinsella's residency at Joyful Noise, Hunky Dory TK samples nothing but [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]]'s Hunky Dory. It plays at Chicago's Museum of Contemporary Art during the David Bowie Is exhibition.

yt: Noisey: 20 years of Joan of Arc (2016)
years.h: Critics split over He's Got the Whole This Land Is Your Land in His Hands
years.p: Some dismissed the Joyful Noise album. Others rank it among Joan of Arc's most ambitious and fully realized experiments.

years.h: Melina Ausikaitis sings, and Winston Smith becomes Tim Kinsella
years.p: Tim Kinsella's description of 1984, where Ausikaitis takes lead vocals on some songs.
years.xp:
Joyful Noise printed a version of Nineteen Eighty-Four set in Chicago, with Winston Smith renamed Tim Kinsella and O'Brien renamed Bobby Burg. It was posted on 1984.com for a limited time.

Kinsella said the record alternates the way a late Black Flag album does: Ausikaitis sings a song, then the band jams.

years.h: Joan of Arc names its last album after its last four members
years.p: Announced September 23, Tim Melina Theo Bobby comes out December 4, 2020, and ends the band after 25 years.
